# Documentation

- [FAQ](https://jazz.tools/docs/faq): Frequently asked questions about Jazz.
- [Overview](https://jazz.tools/docs): The database that syncs.
- [Quickstart](https://jazz.tools/docs/quickstart): Scaffold a synced local-first app in one command.
- [Authentication](https://jazz.tools/docs/auth/authentication): How and when to use Jazz's auth modes, and how to manage JWT auth over the lifetime of a live client.
- [Lifecycle](https://jazz.tools/docs/auth/lifecycle): Client auth lifecycle: local-first identity storage, sign-in and sign-out, storage reset, and upgrading to external auth.
- [Local-first auth](https://jazz.tools/docs/auth/local-first-auth): Authenticate users without a server using self-signed tokens, and optionally upgrade to an external provider while preserving identity.
- [Permissions](https://jazz.tools/docs/auth/permissions): Jazz's approach to row-level security using relationship-based access controls, and how to build policies of varying complexity.
- [Sessions](https://jazz.tools/docs/auth/sessions): Reading the current session and scoping queries and inserts to the logged-in user.
- [Branches](https://jazz.tools/docs/concepts/branches): How Jazz uses branches to isolate data across environments, schema versions, and user-defined contexts.
- [How Sync Works](https://jazz.tools/docs/concepts/how-sync-works): An overview of how Jazz syncs data between clients, covering query subscriptions, infrastructure tiers, offline behavior, and eventual consistency.
- [Local-First Data Model](https://jazz.tools/docs/concepts/local-first-data-model): An overview of how Jazz manages local state, row histories, conflicts, and loading behavior.
- [Client Setup](https://jazz.tools/docs/getting-started/client-setup): Set up Jazz in your app — works out of the box with most frameworks, with manual configuration available when needed.
- [Server Setup](https://jazz.tools/docs/getting-started/server-setup): Hosted and self-hosted database server configuration, app provisioning, and backend context setup.
- [Client](https://jazz.tools/docs/install/client): Build a local-first to-do app with Jazz, step by step.
- [TypeScript Server](https://jazz.tools/docs/install/typescript-server): Build a server-side to-do API with Jazz and Hono, step by step.
- [Filters, Sorting & Pagination](https://jazz.tools/docs/reading/filters-and-sorting): Filter rows with where(), sort with orderBy(), and paginate with limit/offset.
- [Includes & Relations](https://jazz.tools/docs/reading/includes-and-relations): Resolve references with include(), pick columns with select(), inspect permissions, and run recursive queries.
- [Queries](https://jazz.tools/docs/reading/queries): One-shot queries, subscriptions, framework hooks, Suspense integration, and read durability options.
- [Durability Tiers](https://jazz.tools/docs/reference/durability-tiers): API reference for read and write durability tiers: the options that control how far data must propagate before an operation confirms.
- [Examples](https://jazz.tools/docs/reference/examples): What each example app in the Jazz monorepo uniquely demonstrates.
- [Framework Patterns](https://jazz.tools/docs/reference/framework-patterns): Side-by-side reference for React/Expo, Vue, Svelte, and Solid Jazz APIs.
- [Inspector](https://jazz.tools/docs/reference/inspector): Standalone admin client for exploring Jazz sync servers, schemas, permissions, and live queries.
- [Advanced Internals](https://jazz.tools/docs/reference/internals): How Jazz works under the hood: raw tables, row histories, sync, the query pipeline, and the browser architecture.
- [Local-first auth internals](https://jazz.tools/docs/reference/local-first-auth-internals): How local-first auth derives a stable account from a secret, how the self-signed JWT is structured, and how the server verifies it without an external key store.
- [MCP Server](https://jazz.tools/docs/reference/mcp): Give your AI assistant direct access to Jazz documentation via the Model Context Protocol.
- [WHERE Operators](https://jazz.tools/docs/reference/where-operators): Full reference for filter operators available in Jazz query builders, with examples for each column kind.
- [Column Types](https://jazz.tools/docs/schemas/column-types): Every column type available in the TypeScript DSL and its SQL equivalent.
- [Defining Tables](https://jazz.tools/docs/schemas/defining-tables): Define tables and relationships in schema.ts using the TypeScript DSL.
- [Migrations](https://jazz.tools/docs/schemas/migrations): Structural schema evolution workflow and reviewed migration edges.
- [Files & Blobs](https://jazz.tools/docs/writing/files-and-blobs): Chunked browser Blob and stream storage using conventional files and file_parts tables.
- [Writing Data](https://jazz.tools/docs/writing/writing-data): Insert, update, and delete APIs with local-first execution, framework context hooks, and an intro to durability tiers.
- [Group permissions](https://jazz.tools/docs/recipes/access-control/group-permissions): Model a workspace with role-based access control using a members table and existence-based permissions.
- [Shared access between users](https://jazz.tools/docs/recipes/access-control/shared-access): Grant other users access to your data using a shares table and existence-based permissions.
- [User-owned data](https://jazz.tools/docs/recipes/access-control/user-owned-data): End-to-end walkthrough of the most common Jazz pattern: data that belongs to the user who created it.
- [Auth provider integration](https://jazz.tools/docs/recipes/auth/auth-provider-integration): Connect an external auth provider to Jazz with JWT validation, with examples for Better Auth and WorkOS.
- [Better Auth Adapter](https://jazz.tools/docs/recipes/auth/better-auth-adapter): Use Better Auth with Jazz as the database adapter.
- [Nested data with permission inheritance](https://jazz.tools/docs/recipes/data-patterns/nested-data): Model a project/task/comment hierarchy with inherited permissions, queries, and multi-level inserts.
- [Real-time collaborative list](https://jazz.tools/docs/recipes/data-patterns/real-time-collaborative-list): Multiple users subscribing to the same data and seeing each other's changes in real-time.
